title: VITA: ViT Acceleration for Efficient 3D Human Mesh Recovery via Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design
problem: Vision Transformer-based 3D Human Mesh Recovery suffers from high computational complexity, substantial memory footprint, and poor data locality, making efficient acceleration for AR/VR applications challenging. Current ViT implementations struggle with compute efficiency and memory access patterns.
motivation: Real-time 3D human mesh recovery is essential for AR/VR applications, which demand both low-latency inference and energy efficiency on edge devices.
method: VITA replaces the computationally expensive multi-head attention mechanism (where a model learns multiple weighted ways to focus on different parts of an image) with average pooling (simply averaging values in local regions) and reorganizes how data flows through memory to reduce expensive lookups. On the hardware side, it designs a specialized accelerator with flexible internal routing that efficiently executes the pooling, normalization (rescaling intermediate results), and convolution operations in the order the new algorithm needs, eliminating wasted cycles from mismatched hardware-algorithm pairs.
key_novelty: Replace computationally expensive multi-head attention with average pooling in Vision Transformers for 3D human mesh recovery, while co-designing hardware to efficiently execute the resulting computation patterns.
contributions: Average pooling model as efficient alternative to multi-head attention
Hardware accelerator architecture supporting flexible dataflows for pooling, normalization, and convolution
Data locality optimization techniques for ViT workloads
Integrated hardware-algorithm co-design framework achieving significant speedups
limitations: Accuracy trade-offs from attention replacement and generalization to other vision transformer tasks not discussed.
primary_theme: Hardware-algorithm co-design for vision transformer acceleration
